prompt: The client asks: "What should we do with our loss-making European division?" Fact sheet: the division lost $20M last year; its revenue has fallen 10% a year for three years; a buyer has offered $50M; restructuring would cost $80M and might break even in three years; the division is 8% of group revenue; its head office is in Paris. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: Sell the European division. It lost $20M last year and revenue is falling 10% a year; a sale brings $50M, while restructuring would cost $80M with break-even at best three years away. The main risk is that the price falls once the buyer sees the declining revenue, so the next step is to start the sale process while the $50M offer stands.
options.feedback: Right. It leads with the answer, backs it with the numbers that matter, and gives a risk and a next step.

options.text: On one hand, it lost $20M last year and revenue is falling 10% a year; a sale brings $50M, while restructuring would cost $80M with break-even at best three years away. On the other hand, there is the risk that the price falls once the buyer sees the declining revenue. It depends on the client's priorities, so I'd want more analysis before committing either way.
